pool.text: Vietnamese Nguyen lords established administrative structures in the area, detaching it from Cambodia.
It served as the capital of the Nguyen lords before the establishment of the Nguyen dynasty.
The Citadel of Saigon fell during the Cochinchina campaign before becoming the French capital.
Gia Dinh Bao was established in Saigon, becoming the first newspaper published in Vietnam.
Bao Dai made Saigon the capital of the State of Vietnam within the French Union.
Buddhist monk Thich Quang Duc self-immolated in the city in protest of the Diem regime.
Communist forces launched a failed attempt to capture the city during the Tet Offensive.
Saigon was captured, ending the Vietnam War and coming under control of the Vietnamese People's Army.
The city of Saigon and other areas were combined to create Ho Chi Minh City.
The Stock Exchange, the first stock exchange in Vietnam, was opened in the city.
Sixty people died and ninety were injured in the International Trade Center building fire.
The Ho Chi Minh City – Trung Luong Expressway was opened, connecting to the Mekong Delta.
A specific location opened to the public as a spot for locals and visitors to gather.
The Saigon Waterbus launched, connecting down town to Thu Duc.
Line 1 was opened in Ho Chi Minh City.
Provinces were merged into Ho Chi Minh City, inheriting industrial and coastal metropolitan areas.
Long Thanh International Airport is scheduled to begin operating.
